messages:
maria: Quick question - should we formalize a cross-project delegation auditflow for leased credentials? sketch below.
jamal: yes please. current ad-hoc mappings are a pain in reviews.
ashley: TL;DR what do you mean by auditflow?
maria: two parts: (1) enforce explicit trust-mapping records for any cross-project delegation, (2) every mint/exchange emits a single, immutable audit entry that links origin_actor, target_project, claim_version, and optional attestation.
sebastian: linking claim_version is good. helps us reconcile role changes. How do we store mapping records? DB vs git-like policy repo?
ravi: prefer a policy store with strict ACLs and UI for approvals. backing store can be a DB with append-only changelog. audit-bot can mirror diffs to immutable storage.
nina: SDK implications: clients need to send origin_project + origin_actor in mint calls. Also add exchange_reason header when converting legacy keys.
jamal: security: automatic legacy-exchange must be explicit opt-in and rate-limited. record exchanged=true in audit entry and avoid implicit exchange for high-priv flows.
ashley: operator pins: require two-step approval (UI + email confirmation) and an attestation token from the orchestration layer. TTL cap 72h.
maria: okay. revocation semantics? emergency vs policy. emergency should be hard and propagate to edges fast. policy revokes can be eventual with claim_version bump.
sebastian: streaming revocation push to edge fleet + local bloom for quick checks seems best. fallback polling every 30s if stream dies. target p99 propagation < 10s for emergency ids.
ravi: note: bloom false positives mean occasional deny; acceptable. track false-positive rate and provide admin override.
nina: what about opaque tokens vs JWTs? opaque + claim_version fast-path still preferred. token carries token_id + claim_version + origin metadata.
jamal: agree. that keeps control. add a small signed attestation blob for pinned leases that edges can validate if present.
ashley: cross-project call handling: receiver must consult mapping; if mapping maps origin_actor->local_alias then enforce local RBAC for the alias. If mapping absent, default deny for protected endpoints. Document mapping lifecycle: create->two-approver->audit.
maria: ops concerns: burst mint load if many short TTLs. add per-project mint quotas and client-side caching; also pre-warm pinned leases during job start.
sebastian: also include a grace-mode: if authz broker is unavailable, edges should allow low-risk read-only calls but deny write/privileged ones. list policy levels: public, protected, critical.
ravi: testing matrix: mint latency bench, revocation propagation, false-positive bloom rate, mapping resolution correctness, legacy-exchange abuse tests.
ops-bot: Reminder - security review required before broad opt-in. File RFC link in the ticket.
audit-bot: Audit requirement: mapping changes, pin approvals, and legacy-exchanges must produce immutable audit entries and be retained for 1 year.
jamal: rollout plan idea: feature-flag broker + SDK opt-in -> small canary -> perf bench -> enable mapping UI -> opt-in exchange for infra -> deprecate legacy keys after 180 days.
maria: I'll write the RFC with recommended defaults and attach runbook snippets for revocation and stream failure. Draft by end of week. :thumbsup:
